svg.text: The six position subtypes — one worked record each (LDM 1.22)
green = position record (BOR-owned) · yellow = its metric rows (engine-written) · orange = what makes this subtype itself
one trade = one position; Position Id = trade id
Legs defined in Product; metric legId points at them. Reference = which trade version the photo captured.
many trades netted into one holding of an instrument
Identity = instrument × book, not a trade. The only subtype where Instrument Identifier is the star.
money sitting in an account — no contract behind it
Simplest citizen: nearly all coordinates empty. Proof the shared spine degrades gracefully.
client money WE owe — the sign flips
Negative PV is correct, not an error: their asset, our liability. Producer = MATNY for its own accruals.
the promise to lend — commitment, not cash
(no NPV row — nothing to discount until drawn)
Subtype attributes appear: Facility Name/Status (1.22). Kept separate from Outstanding to avoid double-count.
the drawn slice of the facility — actual money out
Facility 100 = Outstanding 40 + Undrawn 60 — two positions, one truth, summable only because they're split.
Reading the set as one lesson
• The green spine is identical six times — id, system, date+snap, book, type — which is why one metric table serves them all.
• What varies is which identity field is the star: trade id (Trade) · instrument×book (Fungible) · account (Cash) · arrangement id + subtype attributes (Deposit/Facility/Outstanding).
• Reference fields matter most where the source record versions (trades, deposits); least where there is no source contract at all (cash).
• Facility/Outstanding is the model's double-count lesson in reference form: aggregate UNDRAWN + drawn NPV only because the subtypes keep them apart.
• Every metric row above lands in the SAME yellow table — subtype of the position never changes the shape of its metrics.
